canonical_name: Lax entropy condition for a shock in a hyperbolic system of conservation laws
canonical_statement: For a discontinuity joining constant left and right states u_L and u_R and moving with speed s in a strictly hyperbolic system u_t + f(u)_x = 0, a Lax k-shock is required to satisfy the Rankine-Hugoniot relation f(u_R) - f(u_L) = s (u_R - u_L) and the characteristic inequalities lambda_k(u_R) < s < lambda_k(u_L), with the adjacent-family inequalities needed to express that all other characteristic families cross the shock in the same direction.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: a finite-dimensional real state space, a differentiable flux f, two states u_L/u_R, shock speed s : Real, an indexed real spectrum of Df at each state, and a family index k. Exact Lean types and universes remain open.
quantifiers: system dimension n and characteristic-family index k
flux f and left/right states u_L, u_R
ordered real eigenvalue branches lambda_i at u_L and u_R
hypotheses: strict hyperbolicity at both states (real, distinct, consistently ordered characteristic speeds)
u_L and u_R are the traces on the designated left and right sides
the selected discontinuity is a k-shock under the source's family-index convention
conclusion: The Lax compressivity inequalities hold: the kth characteristic speed is above s on the left and below s on the right, together with the convention-dependent adjacent-family inequalities/full incoming-characteristic count.

excluded_degenerate_cases: This intake excludes scalar Oleinik/Kruzkov entropy conditions, undercompressive and overcompressive shocks, non-strictly-hyperbolic states, rarefaction admissibility, and a theorem asserting existence or uniqueness of entropy solutions. Endpoint families k=1 and k=n require one-sided adjacent clauses rather than fictitious eigenvalues.
